deities: Shiva (Mahadeva, east-facing; manifested as Nataraja per temple lore)

history.summary: Ancient Shiva-Parvathy temple at Kaloor, Ernakulam. Legend (keralatourism.org): a hunting couple found remnants of an old temple here; astrologers divined a self-evolved (swayambhu) divine power of Shiva, with the presiding deity manifested as Nataraja. Shiva faces east, Parvathi west; sub-deities include Ayyappa, Ganapathi, Murugan, Chamundi, Nagaraja and Dakshinamoorthi. The temple was modest until around 2005, after which it grew wealthy and busy, starting daily annadana; visitor reviews say it is managed by a trust associated with the VHP. Founding date and dynasty are UNVERIFIED; treat the 'ancient' origin as traditional legend.

name: Kaloor Pavakulam Sree Mahadeva Kshetram
town_description: Kaloor is a busy urban hub in Kochi, Kerala's commercial capital and port city on the Malabar Coast. Kochi blends Dutch, Portuguese and British colonial heritage with a thriving modern cityscape, including the Fort Kochi and Mattancherry historic quarters and the Marine Drive waterfront. The temple sits in a dense city neighbourhood near Kaloor junction.

travel.road: Kaloor is inside Kochi city with good road connectivity; the temple is near Kaloor junction on Little Flower Church Road
